items.title: Coroutines
items.sub: Prepared work and a switch point

slides.title: Coroutine
slides.main: Calling an async function does not run the body: it returns a coroutine to be started.

body.text:
import asyncio

async def hello(name):
    return f"hello, {name}"

coro = hello("Anna")
print(type(coro).__name__)
print(asyncio.run(coro))

slides.title: await and asyncio.sleep
slides.main: time.sleep inside an async function freezes the whole event loop: use asyncio.sleep.

body.text:
import asyncio
import time

async def main():
    start = time.perf_counter()
    await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
    await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
    return time.perf_counter() - start

print(asyncio.run(main()) >= 0.2)
Two awaits in a row run in sequence: to overlap jobs you need tasks.

slides.title: Tasks
slides.main: Three 0.2 s waits overlap: about 0.2 s instead of 0.6. Keep a reference to the task.

body.text:
import asyncio
import time

async def job(name, delay):
    await asyncio.sleep(delay)
    return name

async def main():
    start = time.perf_counter()
    tasks = [asyncio.create_task(job(n, 0.2)) for n in "abc"]
    results = [await t for t in tasks]
    return results, time.perf_counter() - start < 0.5

print(asyncio.run(main()))

slides.title: gather
slides.sub: Results come in the order passed
slides.main: return_exceptions=True turns errors into result items: you handle them.

body.text:
import asyncio

async def fetch(n):
    await asyncio.sleep(0.3 - n * 0.1)
    if n == 2:
        raise ValueError("failure")
    return n * 10

async def main():
    print(await asyncio.gather(fetch(0), fetch(1)))
    res = await asyncio.gather(*(fetch(n) for n in range(4)), return_exceptions=True)
    print(res)

asyncio.run(main())

slides.title: Timeout and cancellation
slides.main: Do not swallow CancelledError; finally also runs on cancel, for cleanup.

body.text:
import asyncio

async def slow():
    try:
        await asyncio.sleep(10)
    finally:
        print("cleanup")

async def main():
    try:
        async with asyncio.timeout(0.1):
            await slow()
    except TimeoutError:
        print("timeout")
    t = asyncio.create_task(slow())
    await asyncio.sleep(0.05)
    t.cancel()
    try:
        await t
    except asyncio.CancelledError:
        print("cancelled", t.cancelled())

asyncio.run(main())

slides.title: TaskGroup
slides.main: One task fails, the rest are cancelled and errors are gathered into a group (except*).

body.text:
import asyncio

async def ok(n):
    await asyncio.sleep(0.05)
    return n

async def bad():
    await asyncio.sleep(0.01)
    raise ValueError("failure")

async def main():
    async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as tg:
        a = tg.create_task(ok(1))
        b = tg.create_task(ok(2))
    print(a.result(), b.result())
    try:
        async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as tg:
            tg.create_task(ok(3))
            tg.create_task(bad())
    except* ValueError as eg:
        print("group:", [str(e) for e in eg.exceptions])

asyncio.run(main())

import asyncio

async def ticker(n):
    for i in range(n):
        await asyncio.sleep(0.01)
        yield i

class Conn:
    async def __aenter__(self):
        print("opened")
        return self
    async def __aexit__(self, *exc):
        print("closed")

async def main():
    async with Conn():
        async for x in ticker(3):
            print(x)
    print([x async for x in ticker(2)])

asyncio.run(main())

slides.title: asyncio.Queue
slides.main: No locks or races: switching happens only at await. maxsize slows the producer.

body.text:
import asyncio

async def worker(name, q, out):
    while True:
        item = await q.get()
        out.append((name, item * 2))
        q.task_done()

async def main():
    q, out = asyncio.Queue(), []
    workers = [asyncio.create_task(worker(n, q, out)) for n in "ab"]
    for i in range(5):
        await q.put(i)
    await q.join()
    for w in workers:
        w.cancel()
    print(sorted(item for _, item in out))

asyncio.run(main())

slides.title: Semaphore
slides.sub: At most N at a time
slides.main: Thread locks do not work here: they block the loop. Use the asyncio versions.

body.text:
import asyncio

active = peak = 0

async def request(sem):
    global active, peak
    async with sem:
        active += 1
        peak = max(peak, active)
        await asyncio.sleep(0.02)
        active -= 1

async def main():
    sem = asyncio.Semaphore(3)
    await asyncio.gather(*(request(sem) for _ in range(10)))
    print(peak)

asyncio.run(main())

slides.title: Blocking code: to_thread
slides.sub: Move it outside the event loop
slides.main: The loop handles waiting; blocking work goes to threads or processes.

body.text:
import asyncio
import time

def blocking():
    time.sleep(0.2)
    return "done"

async def main():
    start = time.perf_counter()
    results = await asyncio.gather(*(asyncio.to_thread(blocking) for _ in range(5)))
    print(results[0], len(results), time.perf_counter() - start < 0.8)

asyncio.run(main())

slides.title: Common mistakes
slides.main: A blocking call in a coroutine lets everyone down; without await a coroutine will not run.

body.text:
import asyncio
import gc
import warnings

async def work():
    return 1

async def main():
    with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as w:
        warnings.simplefilter("always")
        work()                       # forgot await
        gc.collect()
    print(len(w) >= 1, "never awaited" in str(w[0].message))
    print(await work())

asyncio.run(main())
Also: asyncio.run inside a loop, a lost task reference, a swallowed CancelledError, thousands of tasks with no limit, waiting without a timeout.

slides.title: Summary
slides.main: The model is cooperative: a coroutine must yield, or it lets everyone down.

items.sub: Do not wait forever; do not swallow cancel
